question: What is vendor-managed inventory?
html:
Vendor-managed inventory (VMI) is an arrangement where we, the supplier, track and replenish a lab's stock of agreed items instead of the lab placing each order itself. In our growth plan, VMI sits alongside punchout ordering and private label as a way to make accounts stickier (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

How it typically works

  • We agree on a list of items and target stock levels with the customer.
  • We monitor usage on site or through the customer's systems.
  • We restock before items run short, so lab staff spend less time ordering.
  • The customer gets steadier supply. We get repeat, predictable volume.

This describes common practice in general. It is not a description of a live Thomas Scientific programme.

Where it fits our plan

LeverRole in the plan
Target-account sellingCoverage of 713 Pursue and 2,317 Nurture sites
Punchout orderingDigital ordering, now table stakes
VMIMakes accounts sticky
Private labelHigher-margin mix

(Thomas Scientific growth plan)

  • The plan says margin has to come from mix, and it names VMI as the stickiness lever (Thomas Scientific growth plan).
  • The plan also calls for AI agents for forecasting. Those could support VMI replenishment (est., inferred link).
  • Named coverage is planned to reach about 1,000 Pursue and Nurture sites by month 12 and about 3,000 by month 36. These are assumptions, not forecasts (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

What we cannot yet say

The context has no VMI-specific figures. It does not show:

  • How many accounts use VMI today.
  • Whether VMI accounts retain better or spend more than non-VMI accounts.
  • What VMI costs to serve, including on-site labour, consigned stock and working capital.

Account-level order history, retention rates by service type and cost-to-serve data would answer these questions. Until then, any VMI impact is an estimate.

Sequencing matters

Every lever is sequenced behind liquidity and refinancing. The first-lien loan matures Dec 14, 2027. Estimated leverage is 7-10x (est., low confidence) (Thomas Scientific public filings). VMI ties up inventory, so its working-capital needs have to fit that constraint.

Sticky, recurring lab accounts strengthen the growth story that BSP needs to earn the refinancing, but only if VMI does not consume cash the business cannot spare.

Next actions

  1. Pull order history to identify which current accounts already behave like VMI candidates, meaning high-frequency, repeat consumables buyers.
  2. Measure retention and cost-to-serve for any existing managed-stock accounts before scaling.
  3. Model the working-capital impact of VMI against the liquidity plan ahead of the Dec 14, 2027 maturity.
  4. Prioritise VMI pilots within the Pursue sites already slated for named coverage.
